subject.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…

question: Should OpenClaw accept this source-layer `provider.model` normalization for persisted memory indexes before broader memory provider auto-detection work lands?
rationale: The patch is narrow and appears correct, but it changes model identity used for memory metadata, provider keys, chunk tags, and vector lookup when adapters return an empty model, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Land after upgrade-aware review
options.body: Accept the backfill if maintainers are satisfied that normalizing empty provider models to the resolved adapter model is the intended upgrade behavior for persisted memory indexes.

options.title: Request full persisted-index proof
options.body: Ask for a live existing-index reindex plus `memory_search` transcript if source inspection, focused tests, and provider-creation proof are not enough for this storage path.

options.title: Pause for broader provider policy
options.body: Hold this PR only if maintainers want provider.model backfill bundled with the auto-provider migration decision tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Land after upgrade-aware review
recommendation.body: Accept the backfill if maintainers are satisfied that normalizing empty provider models to the resolved adapter model is the intended upgrade behavior for persisted memory indexes.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz authored the current memory index identity validation behavior that this provider.model normalization feeds.
